column1: # Hand-written: codes WUGrid runs into while probing, explained from real runs (docs/FIELD-NOTES.md). Edit freely.
# Same columns as error-codes.microsoft.tsv; both files are loaded and every match is shown.

column4: The servicing session is corrupt: at boot CBS found a stale, half-applied package session and discarded it. Seen when several months of cumulative updates were staged on top of each other without a restart: only the oldest committed, the rest failed (CBS.log: "Stale uno package session found", "Failed to resume session"). The server comes back looking clean, but at an old patch level.
column5: Compare the build (UBR) with the one you expected. Install the latest cumulative update again and restart. CBS.log is at \\<server>\admin$\Logs\CBS\CBS.log.

column4: Access is denied. While a server restarts this is usually temporary: RPC answers before Windows security and WMI are ready. On a server that is up and settled it means your account is not an administrator there, or DCOM/WMI remote permissions block it.
column5: If the server is restarting, wait a few minutes. Otherwise check that your account is in the server's local Administrators group and that remote DCOM/WMI access is allowed.

column4: The RPC server is unavailable: nothing answered on RPC. Usual while a server is shutting down or booting. On a running server: a firewall blocks RPC/DCOM (TCP 135 plus the dynamic RPC ports), the WMI service is not running, or the name resolves to a different machine.
column5: If the server is restarting, wait. Otherwise check the firewall rules "Windows Management Instrumentation (DCOM-In)" and "(WMI-In)", and that the name resolves to the right address.

column4: The remote procedure call failed mid-call: the connection dropped, typically because the server started shutting down.
column5: Usually transient during a restart; the next poll reconnects.

column4: The RPC endpoint mapper answered but the requested interface is not registered yet: the WMI service is still starting.
column5: Usually transient while the server boots.

column4: A system shutdown is in progress.
column5: Transient: the server is going down for the restart.

column4: The network path was not found: SMB (TCP 445) does not answer, or the name does not reach the server.
column5: Check that "File and Printer Sharing (SMB-In)" is allowed on the server's firewall and that the name resolves.

column4: The network name cannot be found: the admin$ share does not exist on the server (administrative shares disabled).
column5: Administrative shares return when AutoShareServer is not 0 under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters and the Server service restarts.

column4: The user name or password is incorrect.
column5: Check the account used to reach the server.

column4: No answer within the time limit.
column5: The server may be overloaded, booting, or a firewall drops the traffic silently. Check again in a minute.

column4: The name does not resolve: DNS has no record for it.
column5: Check the spelling, try the fully qualified name, or check which DNS suffixes this workstation searches.

column4: The restart was refused because users are signed in to the server. Windows refuses a restart that is not forced while anyone has a session there, active or disconnected (closing a Remote Desktop window leaves its session signed in); only a forced restart would sign them out, and WUGrid never forces one. Since 0.8.0 WUGrid reads the sessions just before sending and skips such a server, naming who is signed in.
column5: Have them sign out, or end the session once its owner agrees: quser /server:<server> lists the sessions with their state and idle time, and logoff <ID> /server:<server> ends one (what is open in it closes without saving). Then send the restart again.
